Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Director
We are a startup with a short operating history.

We were formed on September 30, 2026 and have a short operating history. We are subject to all of the risks inherent in the establishment of a new business venture. You should consider the likelihood of our success in light of the problems, expenses, difficulties, complications, uncertainties and delays that are frequently encountered in the formation of a new business. A significant amount of our activity is focused on raising capital and growing Pacioli. We cannot assure you that we will succeed.

Our success depends on our ability to attract Users. Our Users are issuers of crypto assets, their advisors and Operators. To attract them, we must ensure that our services are secure, reliable and engaging, and we must expand and evolve those services. We cannot assure you that we will be able to do so. Each of the following can negatively affect adoption: changes in sentiment about the quality or usefulness of Pacioli; concerns about privacy or security; a failure to introduce products that are adopted; and adverse changes mandated by legislation, regulators or litigation.
Our management may allocate time to other activities, causing conflicts of interest.

Mr. Meyers, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, is also Lead Architect of Auditchain, the licensor of Pacioli, and controls both Auditchain and us. He and our other management and development personnel may be engaged in other projects and business endeavors. They are not obligated to contribute any specific number of hours per week to our affairs. If their other business affairs require them to devote more substantial amounts of time to those affairs, their ability to devote time to us could be limited. That could have a negative impact on our ability to operate efficiently.
We depend on the Auditchain License and may face intellectual property claims.

We license Pacioli from Auditchain, an affiliate under common control with us, under the Auditchain License. Mr. Meyers controls both Auditchain and us. The Auditchain License is perpetual, global and exclusive and includes the right to sublicense. We do not own Pacioli. We pay Auditchain a royalty of 20 percent of our revenue, in whatever form we receive it, excluding the proceeds of our offerings. The royalty reduces the amount that remains for our operations.

The PVN software is not open source. Auditchain remains our licensor after the filing of Form TR. A holder of a Node License may run any version of the PVN software that passes Conformance Validation. However, a new version exists only if Auditchain, we or another person changes the code under the Business Source License 1.1. If none of them does, the PVN software may not keep pace with new reporting schemes or with defects that are found.

We are not aware of any violation of the intellectual property rights of others. However, we may face claims that Pacioli or its commercial use infringes the rights of others. If we were found to be infringing, we could face significant costs to implement work-arounds, the need to license a third party's intellectual property on terms that might not be available, substantial monetary judgments or an injunction. Those consequences might cause us to cease operations. Even claims without merit would require our management to dedicate substantial time to them.
Our results depend on sales of Units, and our operating expenses will increase.

Our revenue consists, and will consist, almost entirely of the proceeds of the Units and the AUDT that we sell in our offerings. We recognize the revenue from a Unit when the Unit has been delivered and the Network operates. The proceeds of our offerings will not recur once our offerings are complete.

We anticipate that our operating expenses will increase substantially as we hire employees, expand business development and marketing, and develop additional products and services. We also anticipate that we will incur significant legal, accounting and other expenses.

After our offerings, our only recurring revenue will be the rewards of the validators that we operate, any rewards that our PVN earns and the preparation costs that Preparers pay us. We have had no revenue from preparation. After the filing of Form TR, we may also earn royalties and revenue from data-analytics tools that we may develop as a third party. That revenue may not be sufficient to offset our expenses.
We depend on the health of the market for crypto assets.

Crypto assets are extremely volatile. The total value of all cryptocurrencies has experienced substantial volatility. A significant level of fraud in cryptocurrencies and digital assets has occurred. If such fraud is deemed prevalent, it could jeopardize the potential for digital asset innovation and cause declines in prices and in overall confidence.

We face a substantially higher risk of failure if the market for cryptocurrencies and digital assets experiences significant future declines. Such volatility and possible fraud may prevent issuers of crypto assets and their advisors from adopting Pacioli. If the market suffers a substantial decline, you may lose all or part of the cost of your purchase.
The value of AUDT depends on the adoption of Pacioli. AUDT has no market, and a listing may not occur.

AUDT is a new token. It is not listed on any trading venue and is not liquid. A market for AUDT has yet to develop.

We intend to seek trading of AUDT on the venues named in the table of trading venues after the filing of Form TR. No venue has agreed to list AUDT. A venue may decline to list AUDT or may delist it. Transfers of AUDT are locked until the day named in the Form TR Signal. Trading before the filing of Form TR would be trading of a CIC that is subject to the securities laws.

Until Pacioli is widely used, we do not expect AUDT to have any value beyond its use on the Network. Until the Handover, we set the amount of AUDT that an Operator must stake and the amount at which the Preparer discount begins. Once Governance Votes open, those amounts may be changed by a Governance Vote together with the approval of the Governance Council. After transfers of AUDT open, the stake of a PVN can be set above 50,000 AUDT. We have not determined what a PVN whose stake is below a higher requirement may then do, or whether and on what terms a PVN can be created after our offerings. Staking by a Preparer is optional. We cannot assure you that participants will accept a staking model. The value of AUDT could be adversely affected if the required staking amounts are high.

If AUDT is not adopted, it will become worthless and you may lose the entire cost of your purchase.
Certain crypto market participants have unrealistic expectations and can spread fear, uncertainty and doubt that could impair the value of AUDT.

Regulatory frameworks for crypto assets are emerging that govern the flow of information and impose consequences for manipulative activities. Nevertheless, certain participants in the crypto asset space have developed unrealistic expectations about access to information, rates of return and the time frame of the returns on crypto assets. A number of factors have contributed to those expectations, including the historical performance of the crypto assets that those participants hold or have held.

These participants may be influential and may have a substantial following among other participants in crypto assets. If any of them holds AUDT and publicly expresses unrealistic opinions, or decides to publicly spread fear, uncertainty and doubt about any aspect of our project, the value of AUDT could decline substantially and you may be negatively affected.
Your AUDT is locked for at least two years, and unstaking deactivates your PVN.

The 50,000 AUDT delivered with each PVN is staked and locked for a minimum of two years. If you unstake, your PVN is deactivated immediately, your Node License ends and your AUDT is released only in equal daily amounts over two years. You may sell a Unit only after two years, only after a new Conformance Validation and only to an Accredited Investor that holds an LEI or a vLEI. If you purchase a Unit without the Node License under the first exception, you may resell it only to a provider of regulatory disclosure management software or services that itself meets the three conditions for such a purchase, which are described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract." You may be unable to sell your Unit when you want to, or at all.
Your stake can be slashed, and restoring it may be costly or impossible for a time.

A PVN that does not undergo its annual Conformance Validation forfeits 10 percent of its existing stake. A PVN that withdraws from a validation request after committing to it forfeits 10 percent of its stake on the first withdrawal and 20 percent on the second withdrawal. On each further withdrawal, it forfeits 30 percent and is deactivated for 30 days. A PVN that does not pass its annual Conformance Validation and does not cure its deficiencies within 30 days is deactivated.

If your stake is reduced, you must restore it. The Smart Contracts set no deadline, and your PVN continues to operate with the reduced stake. Until transfers of AUDT open, you can restore it only with AUDT that you have earned on the Network, by purchasing an additional Unit without the Node License in a Node Offering that is open, at the full price of a Unit, or by purchasing AUDT in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering while it is open. From the end of the Tier 2 AUDT Offering until transfers of AUDT open, you cannot buy AUDT at all. After transfers of AUDT open, AUDT may cost more.
The development of Pacioli will need substantial additional capital.

The development of Pacioli is a highly complex and costly effort that requires substantial capital and support from third parties. To continue development, we must raise substantial additional capital, or third parties must make substantial contributions without cost to us. We cannot assure you that we will be able to raise additional capital, or that third parties will provide such contributions, on reasonable terms or at all. If we do not raise substantial additional capital, we may have to reduce or discontinue development and you may lose all or part of the cost of your purchase.

At August 31, 2027, we had cash of approximately $1,754,000. At our planned rate of spending, that cash funds our operations for approximately three months without the proceeds of this Offering. This Offering will commence only upon the final adoption of Reg CA or under no-action relief, and it has no minimum offering amount.
Pacioli is a complex project without precedent, and we depend on developers and third parties.

Pacioli is unprecedented. It involves a high degree of technical complexity, community coordination and risk management. We depend on the services of the development team and on third parties to develop or provide components. We may face unexpected complexity or delays. Third parties may experience delays or may be unable to deliver to specification. In either case, we will not be able to grow the Network in a timely manner. That may have a material negative effect on our operations, and you may lose all or part of the cost of your purchase.
We depend on standard setters to serve as MCVs, and the MCVs have interests of their own.

A PVN can be admitted to the Network, and can remain on it, only after the initial and annual Conformance Validations performed by the MCVs. Two standard setters serve as the initial MCVs. If they, or other standard setters that later serve as MCVs, cease to serve or delay their Conformance Validations, PVNs cannot be admitted or may be slashed, and the Network may not operate.

The MCVs set the fees for Conformance Validations, and this document does not state their amounts. This document sets no limit on those fees. The MCVs receive one half of every penalty that is taken from the stake of a PVN, including the penalty for a missed annual Conformance Validation, which the MCVs or their delegates perform. An MCV could therefore gain from its own delay.

The MCVs will also hold seats on the Governance Council. While two MCVs sit, neither can be removed, and no further MCV can be admitted, without the approval of one of them. Before Governance Votes open, no person holds a right to admit or remove an MCV.
We face risks related to theft and hacking.

Hackers or other groups, organizations or countries may attempt to interfere with the development, testing, deployment and operation of our project and of AUDT in any number of ways. These include denial-of-service attacks, Sybil attacks, spoofing, smurfing, malware attacks and consensus-based attacks. The Underlying Networks are susceptible to attacks on their consensus, including double-spend and majority attacks. Such attacks would affect the proper execution and sequencing of smart contracts. We may not be able to recover from any such attack, and you may lose all or part of the cost of your purchase.
The source code of the Smart Contracts and of the PVN software is public, and the Security Audit does not eliminate the risk of defects.

The Smart Contracts are open source, and the source code of the PVN software is public under the Business Source License 1.1. Our team or third parties may intentionally or unintentionally introduce weaknesses or bugs into the source code. Those weaknesses or bugs could interfere with the use of Pacioli or cause the loss of AUDT or of any other asset at stake. Ironvault Security Labs completed the Security Audit before deployment, but an audit cannot find every defect. The Governance Contract, the Council Contract, the Scheme Registry and the Consultation Stake Contract, and the changes that they require in the other Smart Contracts, were not covered by the Security Audit. A second audit will cover them before they are deployed, and it also cannot find every defect. The lack of registered intellectual property protection also poses a risk that third parties may file patents and trademarks for substantially similar designs.
Advances in cryptography and computer science could undermine the networks that we use.

Advances in cryptography and cryptanalysis, or technical advances such as the development of quantum computers, could present risks to crypto assets and to the networks and applications that we use. Those risks could result in the theft or loss of crypto assets, including AUDT. The integrity of every blockchain depends on the cryptographic security of its hash functions. There is no scientific assurance that commonly deployed hash functions have that security.
Reg CA has not been adopted.

Reg CA is a proposed rule. This Offering will commence only upon the final adoption of Reg CA by the Commission, or under no-action relief that we may seek in order to conduct this Offering under the proposed rule as published. The Commission may adopt Reg CA in a different form or with different conditions, or may not adopt it at all. No-action relief may not be granted. Our obligations under Reg CA, and your rights, may differ from those described in this document.

In the proposing release, the Commission considered, as an alternative condition of the safe harbor of Rule 400, a test of the functionality of the crypto asset and of the decentralization of its network. It did not propose that test. It asked for comment on other conditions for the safe harbor and on the alternatives that it discussed. A final rule with such a test could require changes to the Governance Council or could delay Form TR. That test is not the meaning that we give to "decentralization" in this document.
Payment in USDC or USDT exposes you and us to stablecoin risks.

Units are paid for in USDC or USDT, each taken at $1.00. We convert USDC and USDT to U.S. dollars on receipt. If a stablecoin loses its peg, is frozen or becomes unusable, purchasers may be unable to pay and we may receive less than $1.00 of value for each USDC or USDT. The proposing release states that the aggregate offering price would include permitted payment stablecoins received for a CIC. It does not state whether a stablecoin is "cash" for the purposes of Reg CA. In this document, we treat USDC and USDT as cash.
There is no minimum offering amount, and we rely on the Placement Agent.

We will begin to use the proceeds of this Offering upon receipt. We cannot assure you that all Units will be sold. If the Placement Agent fails to perform, sales may be slower than planned. If we do not raise the maximum amount, we may not be able to carry out our plan of development as described, and we may reallocate the use of the proceeds.
Purchases are made through smart contracts and wallets, which are vulnerable to attacks.

Smart contracts are subject to errors and attacks. Errors and attacks may cause smart contracts to fail or may cause the loss of the funds collected in this Offering. The wallet addresses that purchasers use are vulnerable to phishing attacks. We do not carry insurance that covers the loss of funds as the result of an attack. If we suffer an attack, we may not be able to reimburse you and you may lose the entire cost of your purchase.
Until the Handover, AUDT for offering deliveries and allocations is minted with our key.

The mint function of the Token Contract is called by the Subsidies Contract, up to 45,000,000 AUDT, for validation rewards and, after the filing of Form TR, for the consultation rewards that the Governance Council may direct. Until the Handover, it is called by the Key Holder Contract, up to 136,083,333 AUDT, for the AUDT delivered in our offerings and for the other allocations. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract also holds the administration key of the Token Contract. That key is not limited to that amount and can give another address a right to mint, within the maximum supply. Until the Governance Contract is deployed, the Key Holder Contract can also upgrade the code of the Smart Contracts. Before the Founding PVNs were admitted, the Key Holder Contract acted on the signatures of two of our three directors alone. If our key and the keys of two other Initial Key Holders were compromised or misused before the Handover, AUDT could be minted, or the Smart Contracts changed, other than as described in this document. That could reduce the value of your AUDT.

After the Handover, AUDT can be minted only by the Subsidies Contract, the Claims Contract and the Council Contract, each within a cap that the Token Contract enforces, up to the maximum supply of 300,000,000 AUDT. No change of code can raise a cap or the maximum supply.
No SOC or ISAE attestation covers the Network, and attestation standards for decentralized networks are unsettled.

Pacioli has no SOC or ISAE attestation. Vendors that provide services on the Network are responsible for obtaining their own attestations. Whether a decentralized network can obtain such an attestation will remain unsettled until the audit standards become clear. Issuers and advisors that require an attested service provider may be unable or unwilling to use the Network. That could slow adoption and reduce the value of AUDT.

We will hold at least 47.1 percent of the AUDT outstanding when we file Form TR, with no lockup other than the lock on transfers of all AUDT and the two-year lock on the 50,000 AUDT staked for our PVN, and our votes can defeat any proposal put to a Governance Vote.

Before the Handover, we will mint to ourselves the remainder of the treasury allocation (56,450,000 AUDT) and the 8,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation for centralized exchanges. We minted the 50,000 AUDT stake of our PVN, which is part of the treasury allocation, when the Token Contract was deployed on July 1, 2027. Together, that AUDT is 64,500,000 AUDT, or 21.50 percent of the maximum supply. The other 12,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation will be locked permanently in the three liquidity contracts, and we will not control it. Our PVN also receives AUDT Subsidies like every other PVN.

Of the treasury allocation, 28,250,000 AUDT is deliverable to Auditchain after the filing of Form TR as consideration for the Auditchain License. Auditchain is a related person and the licensor of Pacioli, and our Chief Executive Officer is its Lead Architect and controls it. After that delivery, we will hold 36,250,000 AUDT, or 12.08 percent of the maximum supply.

No lockup or release schedule applies to any of this AUDT, other than the lock on transfers of all AUDT until the day named in the Form TR Signal and the two-year lock on the 50,000 AUDT staked for our PVN. Sales or other dispositions of this AUDT by us or by Auditchain could reduce the price of AUDT if a market develops.

We and Auditchain will hold a larger share of the AUDT outstanding than of the maximum supply, because AUDT is minted only as it is distributed. No more than 137,083,333 AUDT will be outstanding when we file Form TR. That is the amount that will be outstanding if all of the Units and AUDT in our three offerings are sold and the AUDT Subsidies that may be paid before the filing of Form TR are paid in full. We will then hold at least 47.1 percent of the AUDT outstanding.

When we file Form TR, if we delegate and vote our 64,500,000 AUDT, we can defeat any proposal put to a Governance Vote. We can also carry any settings proposal, and any general proposal unless more than 32,250,000 votes are cast against it. That is more than 53 percent of all the AUDT that other holders will then hold. It is a larger share of the votes that they can cast for as long as the release contract holds AUDT sold in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, because that AUDT carries no vote. While the 8,000,000 AUDT for centralized exchanges is on an exchange, it carries no vote, and we can cast 56,500,000 votes. We cannot carry out a proposal without the approval of the Governance Council, which is the only check on our votes, and we cannot block a mint from the reserve. If we do not vote during the voting period of approximately 2.4 days, other holders can pass a proposal with votes in favor equal to 4 percent of the AUDT outstanding, if the Governance Council approves it. The AUDT that we may award from the team and advisor allocations, up to 60,000,000 AUDT, may add to the votes of persons who vote with us, and AUDT that we buy back adds to our own votes. After the delivery to Auditchain, the same is true of us and Auditchain together.
The validators that we operate or intend to operate on Ethereum and Polygon PoS can be slashed, and their rewards are small and variable.

We and our affiliate Auditchain each operate one validator on Ethereum and intend to operate one validator on Polygon PoS and a full node on Robinhood Chain. A validator that is offline or misbehaves can be penalized or slashed under the rules of those networks. A penalty or slashing would reduce the ETH that we stake or the POL that we intend to stake. Validator rewards depend on network conditions and on the prices of ETH and POL, which we do not control. Validation on Robinhood Chain is permissioned. We intend to apply to its validator allowlist, and our application may not be accepted. These activities are small relative to our business. A loss of the staked assets would not affect the operation of Pacioli.
The Governance Council may not be seated as planned, and we cannot file Form TR until it is.

Our final promised effort includes seating a first Governance Council of at least five members, none of whom is our affiliate, founder, director, officer, employee or adviser. We expect them to be the two initial MCVs and three Operators that the PVNs elect. The standard setters that serve as MCVs may decline their seats, and the PVNs may not elect three eligible members. Until the first Governance Council is seated, we cannot carry out the Handover or file Form TR, transfers of AUDT remain locked and we will not seek a listing.
A Governance Vote and the Governance Council must both approve every change to the Smart Contracts, and they may not agree.

Once Governance Votes open, the code and the settings of the Smart Contracts can be changed only by a Governance Vote together with the approval of the Governance Council. Either can refuse. In a Governance Council of five members, any two can block a change of code. If the approvals are not given, the Smart Contracts continue to run as written: a defect stays in place, and rules that no longer fit cannot be changed.
After the Handover, no one can fix a defect quickly, and a defect in the governing contracts could be permanent.

The Governance Council can pause a Smart Contract but cannot change its code. A fix requires a general proposal: a Governance Vote with two-thirds of the votes cast in favor and the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council. It takes at least approximately 4.4 days, and the contract may be paused in the meantime. The Governance Contract, with its timelock, and the Council Contract cannot be paused. If a defect stopped them from working, no Smart Contract could be changed and the defect could not be fixed. From the deployment of the Governance Contract until Governance Votes open, no one can change the code of the Smart Contracts at all. In that time, a contract with a defect can only be paused.
The Governance Council can pause the Smart Contracts and stop all transfers of AUDT.

After the Handover, more than half of the members of the Governance Council, from at least two of its groups, can pause a Smart Contract. Two-thirds are needed to pause the Token Contract, which stops every transfer of AUDT, the Scheme Registry, which stops the filing of reporting schemes, or the Consultation Stake Contract. The Governance Contract and the Council Contract cannot be paused. Without a Governance Vote, pauses can last up to 14 days in any 90 days, and longer if a pause begins before Governance Votes open. During a pause, you may be unable to transfer, stake, unstake or claim AUDT, or to have a disclosure validated. A pause could coincide with the first listing of AUDT. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract can pause a Smart Contract, and those limits do not apply to it.
The Governance Council can freeze the AUDT at an address.

Upon a demand from law enforcement or an order of a court, two-thirds of the Governance Council can freeze the AUDT at one address, or one stake, for 90 days, and can renew the freeze once. Frozen AUDT cannot be transferred. The Smart Contracts cannot verify that a demand or an order exists or is valid. That depends on the members. The Governance Council could freeze AUDT by mistake or wrongly. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract can freeze AUDT upon such a demand or order. The limits that apply to the Governance Council do not apply to it, and a freeze that it has placed ends at the Handover.
The Commission or others may dispute our Form TR, and AUDT could remain subject to the securities laws.

In Form TR, we will certify that we have completed or permanently ceased all of the essential managerial efforts that we promised. We will also certify that we are not making, and do not intend to make, any new promise of essential managerial efforts with respect to AUDT. Neither the Commission nor its staff is required to review Form TR. The Commission or another party could later dispute our certification. It could point to our voting power, to the AUDT that we may still award, to the preparation costs that we charge, to the vLEIs that we issue and to the licenses that we and Auditchain keep. If we did not satisfy the conditions, the Commission may take the position that the investment contract has not ceased to exist and that the requirements of the securities laws continue to apply.
The Handover cannot be undone. If we do not file Form TR after it, no one can change the Smart Contracts.

At the Handover, we give up our keys to the Smart Contracts. Governance Votes open only when the Form TR Signal takes effect. From the deployment of the Governance Contract, no one can change the code of the Smart Contracts or the allocation of rewards, and from the Handover no one can change any other setting, until Governance Votes open. After the Handover, the Governance Council can only pause and freeze. If we did not file Form TR, that would continue without end, and we could not take our keys back. If the Form TR Signal took effect and Form TR was not filed, or was later withdrawn or denied, AUDT Subsidies above 1,000,000 AUDT, claims and, on the day named in the Form TR Signal, transfers of AUDT would be open although the investment contract still existed.
A few persons will hold the powers of the Governance Council, and they have interests of their own.

We expect the first Governance Council to have five members. Three of them, from both groups, can pause a Smart Contract. Four of them can pause the Token Contract, freeze AUDT and, together with a Governance Vote, change any code. MCVs and Operators earn fees and rewards on the Network and may prefer rules that increase them. The two initial MCVs received their stakes from us without cost. The owner of more than one-quarter of the PVNs can be sure of electing one of the three Operator members, and the owner of more than three-quarters can elect all three. A member that records nothing for 90 days is no longer counted, which lowers the number of approvals needed.
If the Governance Council falls below four members, our votes will decide who fills its empty seats.

The Governance Council can act only while at least four members from at least two of its three groups sit. Otherwise it cannot approve, pause or freeze, and no Smart Contract can be changed. If fewer than four members have sat for 90 days, more than half of the remaining members may name firms for the empty seats, and the holders of AUDT confirm them in a Governance Vote. For as long as we can carry that Governance Vote, we decide whether those firms are seated.
The professional services firms and the regulators that we describe may never take a seat.

Three seats are reserved for professional services firms, and regulators may take observer seats without a vote. No firm and no regulator has agreed to take a seat. The members elect firms by two-thirds approval and may elect none. The Governance Council may consist only of standard setters and Operators.
The legal form of the Governance Council is not settled, and its members may face liability.

We have not determined the legal form of the Governance Council or where it will be organized. Its seats are unpaid, and we will not fund it after the Handover. Its members could face liability, or duties under the laws of several countries, when they pause a contract or freeze AUDT. They may resign or decline to act.
Reporting schemes are added to the Network without a vote, and a faulty or false reporting scheme could be accepted.

Once the Scheme Registry is deployed, a reporting scheme, or a change to one, is filed by its source or its developer. It takes effect after a consultation period of 60 days if it passes the scheme tests, or if no result is reported in time. A version that fails a test is held back for 14 days and then takes effect unless two-thirds of the Governance Council refuse it. An urgent correction takes effect before comment. No one votes on a reporting scheme. Two-thirds of the Governance Council can refuse or pause it only for a stated fault, which the Smart Contracts cannot verify. A reporting scheme could be filed under a false source, could contain errors, or could be set up to collect royalties and AUDT Subsidies on its own traffic. Two-thirds of the Governance Council could also keep a sound reporting scheme out, and an MCV could delay one for 14 days by reporting a failure that is not one.
The Governance Council may pay AUDT to commenters out of the AUDT Subsidies, and it is not obliged to pay anything.

After the filing of Form TR, two-thirds of the Governance Council may direct the Subsidies Contract to pay consultation rewards to persons who lock AUDT during a consultation period and whose comments are taken up. Those payments come out of the 45,000,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies and reduce what remains for validation rewards. They cannot exceed 4,500,000 AUDT in total unless a general proposal changes that ceiling. Within that ceiling, we write the limits on these payments, including their total, and the minimum stake into the code before the Handover. We have not yet set them. After the Handover, the decisions are not ours. The Governance Council decides whether to pay, how much within the limits, and to whom. It may pay nothing, and the members that the PVNs elect have an interest in keeping AUDT Subsidies for validation rewards. Its decisions could favor some commenters, and commenters and filers could act together to obtain rewards. Where our affiliate Auditchain files a reporting scheme, its answer states which comments were taken up. A commenter has no right to a consultation reward.
Until the Handover, our keys are held with four other key holders, and they could block us.

Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract holds the key that mints AUDT, the administration key of the Token Contract and the rights to pause and to freeze. Three of the five Initial Key Holders must sign, and we must be one of them. We cannot act without two of the four other Initial Key Holders. If three of them refused to sign, we could not deliver AUDT that we have sold, mint the liquidity and treasury allocations or carry out the Handover, and we could not file Form TR. From the deployment of the Smart Contracts until the four other Initial Key Holders took up their keys, we held every key alone.
You cannot transfer AUDT until the day named in the Form TR Signal, and that day may not bring a listing.

Transfers of AUDT from one wallet to another are locked until the day that we name in the Form TR Signal. Until then, you can use AUDT only within the Smart Contracts, and you cannot sell it. We do not know when we will file Form TR, and we may never file it. We do not intend to file it before our offerings have ended. We name the day on which we intend AUDT to be listed, but no venue has agreed to list AUDT. The lock ends on that day whether or not AUDT is listed. Once the Form TR Signal has taken effect, we cannot change the day.
Until the Handover, we alone set what a PVN earns.

Until the Governance Contract is deployed, we alone set the allocation of rewards, which includes the rate of AUDT Subsidies and the division of each validation fee among its recipients, and until the Handover, we alone set the other settings of the Smart Contracts. We can change each of them at any time until then. A change can raise or lower the rate of AUDT Subsidies, the fee that a User pays for a validation and the share of that fee that an Operator receives. The table of network reward allocation states the division in force at the date of this document. You can read the division in force from the blockchain, but you cannot rely on it remaining in force. The Subsidies Contract can pay no more than 1,000,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies before the filing of Form TR, and it had paid 100,000 AUDT of them by August 31, 2027. It splits the rest equally each month among the active PVNs, as described under "Plan of development," so that the share of each PVN falls as more PVNs become active, and a PVN that is not active in a month receives none for that month. This document does not state the amount of the fee that a User pays for a validation. Until the Tier 2 AUDT Offering opens, a User that does not operate a PVN cannot obtain AUDT, so that a validation can be paid for in AUDT only by a person that has received AUDT as AUDT Subsidies or as a reward. We have not filed an offering statement for the Tier 2 AUDT Offering. Until that offering opens and we file Form TR, your PVN may earn little or nothing. The shares of each validation fee for liquidity, governance staking, and airdrops and grants are held in the Smart Contracts, and their use will be decided only after the filing of Form TR.
An individual who operates a PVN depends on a vLEI that we issue.

An individual who operates a PVN, or who buys a Unit from an Operator, must hold a vLEI that we issue. We must issue it to every individual who completes identity verification (KYC/AML). We may refuse or revoke it only if the individual fails identity verification or ceases to operate a PVN, or if an order of a court or of a regulator, or a rule of the vLEI system, requires it. If we failed to issue vLEIs, or ceased to exist, individuals could not become Operators and an Operator could not sell a Unit to an individual.
PVNs may not accept AUDT as payment, and AUDT may not be adopted as a means of settlement on Pacioli.

Users pay the PVNs for validations in AUDT, through the Smart Contracts, and/or in other digital assets that the PVNs accept as payment. Each PVN decides which digital assets it accepts. There can be no assurance that PVNs, Users or other participants in Pacioli will accept or use AUDT as a means of settlement. If PVNs choose to be paid in other digital assets, fewer validation fees may be paid in AUDT, demand for AUDT may be lower than we expect and the value of AUDT may decline. You may lose all or part of the cost of your purchase.
The Governance Council can mint up to 58,916,667 AUDT after the Handover, 28,916,667 AUDT of it without a Governance Vote, which would dilute every holder.

After the Handover, the Council Contract can mint the reserve of 28,916,667 AUDT on the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council alone, with no Governance Vote, and the partnership allocation of 30,000,000 AUDT after a Governance Vote. Mints from the reserve could add up to 21 percent to the 137,083,333 AUDT that will be outstanding when we file Form TR, and mints from both up to 43 percent. The Governance Council decides the amount, the timing and the purpose of each mint from the reserve, and neither our votes nor those of other holders can block one. Its members include Operators, whose PVNs may benefit from incentives paid to PVNs, although no AUDT may be minted to a member, to its organization or to an affiliate of either. Mints could reduce the value of AUDT and the share of the votes held by every holder, including us. Bridged AUDT on Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain is created by the bridge of each network. A failure or exploit of a bridge could create AUDT on that network that is not backed by AUDT locked on Ethereum.
The AUDT and USDC that we commit to liquidity pools are locked permanently, and the pools and exchanges may not provide an orderly market.

We will commit 12,000,000 AUDT and $18,000,000 of USDC to Uniswap pools on Ethereum, Robinhood Chain and Polygon PoS, through three liquidity contracts from which no one can withdraw. That USDC comes from the net proceeds of the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, and we will never recover it, whatever happens to the price of AUDT or to the pools. As AUDT is bought and sold in a pool, the mix of AUDT and USDC in it changes, and the value of the position may fall. The pools open at $1.50 per AUDT, the price in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering; they do not support that price. We will also hold 8,000,000 AUDT and $12,000,000 of USDC in our accounts at Coinbase, Kraken and OKX if they list AUDT. That AUDT remains under our control, and an exchange could fail, freeze our account or decline to list AUDT.
Minted to the Company before the Handover. Subject to the lock on transfers of all AUDT until the day named in the Form TR Signal. No other lockup or release schedule applies.

The Council Contract on Ethereum, from the Handover: for the reserve, on the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council; for the partnership allocation, after a general proposal to mint a stated portion passes a Governance Vote and receives the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council.

Calls the mint function of the Token Contract, up to 58,916,667 AUDT in total: 28,916,667 AUDT from the reserve and 30,000,000 AUDT from the partnership allocation. Each mint names the amount, the purpose and the receiving contract, which may be a contract that the Governance Council deploys for bounties, incentives or another purpose. No AUDT may be minted to a member of the Governance Council, its organization or an affiliate of either, to the Company or to Auditchain.
Bridged AUDT on Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain
The bridge of each of those networks.
Creates bridged AUDT on that network only when the same amount of AUDT is locked on Ethereum, and removes it when it returns. It does not change the AUDT outstanding.
No one. None of the three liquidity contracts has a key.

When transfers of AUDT open, any person may call each liquidity contract to deposit its AUDT and USDC in its Uniswap AUDT/USDC pool at $1.50 per AUDT. The contract holds the pool position permanently: no person can withdraw the AUDT or the USDC. It collects the trading fees that the position earns and pays them to the Company.

Decentralized exchange; any wallet. This is an intended venue. The Company intends to seek trading of AUDT on this venue three business days after it files Form TR (January 4, 2029 in the timeline of this demonstration). No venue has agreed to list AUDT, and AUDT is not listed on any venue at the date of this document. The liquidity contract on Polygon PoS will deposit 2,000,000 AUDT and $3,000,000 of USDC in this pool at $1.50 per AUDT when transfers of AUDT open, and will hold that position permanently.

Until the Governance Contract is deployed, we set the allocation of rewards: the division of each validation fee shown in this table, the amount of the rewards paid through AUDT Subsidies and the allocation of the proceeds from data subscriptions. We can change it at any time until then. From the deployment of the Governance Contract, the allocation of rewards, including AUDT Subsidies, is subject to governance. We can no longer change it, and no person can change it until Governance Votes open. After that, it can be changed only by a settings proposal that passes a Governance Vote of the holders of AUDT and receives the ordinary approval of the Governance Council, within the range that the Smart Contracts fix for each setting. The allocation in force can be read from the blockchain.

The Company alone, until the deployment of the Governance Contract, on the signatures of two of its three directors. From that deployment until Governance Votes open: no person. Once Governance Votes open: a Governance Vote together with the ordinary approval of the Governance Council, within the range fixed for each setting.

Change the division of each validation fee among its recipients, which the table of network reward allocation states, the amount of the rewards paid through AUDT Subsidies, which the Subsidies Contract mints, and the allocation of the proceeds from data subscriptions between reporting entities and the PVNs in a cohort.
